result:
The proposed answer, λ, cannot be right, because a probability cannot exceed 1 while λ ranges over (0,∞). The justification given ("the limiting probability is exactly λ") is asserted without any derivation.

A heuristic derivation gives a different answer. A code with generator matrix G is MDS exactly when every k×k minor of G is nonzero, which is a condition over all C(n,k) choices of k columns. For a uniformly random code, each such set of columns is linearly dependent with probability about 1/q. The expected number of dependent k-subsets is therefore about (1/q)·C(n,k) → λ.

When k/n → 0, the dependencies among these events become weak. The number of dependent k-subsets should then be asymptotically Poisson with mean λ. This is the standard heuristic and I am relying on it rather than a full proof. The probability of having no dependent k-subset, which is the probability of being MDS, then tends to e^{-λ}.

So the correct limit is e^{-λ}, not λ.

VERDICT: REJECT
